1. Overview & Base URL

The Payments API lets you accept payments, manage customers and saved payment methods, issue refunds, and receive real-time event notifications. It is organized around REST: resources have predictable URLs, requests and responses use JSON, and standard HTTP verbs and status codes are used throughout.

Base URLs

EnvironmentBase URLKey prefix
Sandbox (testing, no real money)https://api.sandbox.example-pay.com/v1sk_test_
Productionhttps://api.example-pay.com/v1sk_live_

Conventions

  • All requests must use HTTPS. Plain HTTP requests are rejected.
  • Send Content-Type: application/json on requests with a body.
  • Amounts are integers in the smallest currency unit (e.g. 2500 = $25.00 USD).
  • Currencies use lowercase ISO 4217 codes (usd, eur, gbp).
  • Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC (e.g. 2026-11-23T10:15:00Z).
  • Object IDs are prefixed strings, such as pay_, cus_, pm_, ref_.
  • List endpoints use cursor pagination via limit (1–100, default 20) and starting_after.

Idempotency

For any POST request, send an Idempotency-Key header (a unique string such as a UUID) to safely retry without creating duplicate charges. Keys are retained for 24 hours. Reusing a key with different parameters returns a 409 error.

2. Authentication

The API uses secret API keys sent as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.

Authorization: Bearer sk_test_YOUR_SECRET_KEY
Key typePrefixUse
Secret key (sandbox)sk_test_Server-side calls against the sandbox
Secret key (production)sk_live_Server-side calls against production
Publishable keypk_test_ / pk_live_Client-side tokenization of card details only
Webhook signing secretwhsec_Verifying webhook signatures
Keep secret keys secret. Never embed sk_ keys in mobile apps, browser code, or public repositories. Load them from environment variables or a secrets manager, and rotate them immediately if exposed.

Getting and rotating keys

  1. Sign in to the Dashboard and open Developers → API Keys.
  2. Create a key for the desired environment and store it securely; the full value is shown only once.
  3. To rotate, create a new key, deploy it, then revoke the old key.

Requests with a missing, malformed, or revoked key return 401 authentication_failed. A valid key without permission for the resource returns 403 permission_denied.

3. Endpoints

All paths are relative to the base URL.

MethodPathDescription
POST/paymentsCreate a payment
GET/paymentsList payments (supports status, customer_id, created_gte filters)
GET/payments/{id}Retrieve a payment
POST/payments/{id}/captureCapture an authorized payment (full or partial)
POST/payments/{id}/cancelCancel an uncaptured payment
POST/refundsRefund a captured payment (full or partial)
GET/refunds/{id}Retrieve a refund
POST/customersCreate a customer
GET/customers/{id}Retrieve a customer
POST/customers/{id}/payment_methodsAttach a tokenized payment method to a customer
DELETE/payment_methods/{id}Detach and delete a saved payment method
POST/webhook_endpointsRegister a webhook endpoint
GET/webhook_endpointsList webhook endpoints
DELETE/webhook_endpoints/{id}Delete a webhook endpoint

Payment object

FieldTypeDescription
idstringUnique identifier, prefixed pay_
objectstringAlways "payment"
amountintegerAmount in the smallest currency unit
currencystringThree-letter ISO currency code, lowercase
statusstringrequires_action, authorized, succeeded, failed, canceled
customer_idstring | nullAssociated customer
payment_method_idstringPayment method used
capture_methodstringautomatic or manual
amount_refundedintegerTotal refunded so far
metadataobjectUp to 20 key/value string pairs
created_atstringISO 8601 creation time

4. Request & Response Examples

4.1 Create a payment

POST /payments

Request body

{
  "amount": 2500,
  "currency": "usd",
  "payment_method_id": "pm_1Nq8XyAb12Cd34",
  "customer_id": "cus_9Lk2PzQw77",
  "capture_method": "automatic",
  "description": "Order #10482",
  "metadata": {
    "order_id": "10482"
  }
}

Response — 201 Created

{
  "id": "pay_3MtwBw2eZvKY",
  "object": "payment",
  "amount": 2500,
  "currency": "usd",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "customer_id": "cus_9Lk2PzQw77",
  "payment_method_id": "pm_1Nq8XyAb12Cd34",
  "capture_method": "automatic",
  "amount_refunded": 0,
  "description": "Order #10482",
  "metadata": {
    "order_id": "10482"
  },
  "created_at": "2026-11-23T10:15:00Z"
}

POST /refunds

Request body

{
  "payment_id": "pay_3MtwBw2eZvKY",

  "reason": "requested_by_customer"

Response — 201 Created

{
  "id": "ref_5Hd8Tn0cPq",
  "object": "refund",
  "payment_id": "pay_3MtwBw2eZvKY",

  "currency": "usd",

  "created_at": "2026-11-23T11:02:41Z"
}

4.3 List payments

GET /payments?limit=2&status=succeeded

{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    { "id": "pay_3MtwBw2eZvKY", "object": "payment", "amount": 2500, "currency": "usd", "status": "succeeded" },
    { "id": "pay_3MtvAa9dYuJX", "object": "payment", "amount": 4200, "currency": "usd", "status": "succeeded" }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "pay_3MtvAa9dYuJX"
}

4.4 Error response

{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "parameter_invalid",
    "message": "amount must be a positive integer.",
    "param": "amount",
    "request_id": "req_8fA2kLm0Qz"
  }
}

Always log the request_id; support uses it to trace requests.

5. curl Examples

Set your key once as an environment variable:

export API_KEY="sk_test_YOUR_SECRET_KEY"
export BASE_URL="https://api.sandbox.example-pay.com/v1"

Create a customer

curl -X POST "$BASE_URL/customers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2a9e-3b7d-4e55-9a0c-1d2e3f4a5b6c" \
  -d '{
    "email": "jane.doe@example.com",
    "name": "Jane Doe"
  }'

Create a payment

curl -X POST "$BASE_URL/payments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 0b8e7c3a-52d1-4f6e-8a9b-7c6d5e4f3a2b" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 2500,
    "currency": "usd",
    "payment_method_id": "pm_1Nq8XyAb12Cd34",
    "customer_id": "cus_9Lk2PzQw77",
    "description": "Order #10482"
  }'

Retrieve a payment

curl "$BASE_URL/payments/pay_3MtwBw2eZvKY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY"

Capture an authorized payment (partial)

curl -X POST "$BASE_URL/payments/pay_3MtwBw2eZvKY/capture" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "amount_to_capture": 1800 }'

Issue a refund

curl -X POST "$BASE_URL/refunds" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: c4d5e6f7-1a2b-4c3d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f" \
  -d '{ "payment_id": "pay_3MtwBw2eZvKY", "amount": 1000 }'

List payments with filters

curl -G "$BASE_URL/payments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "status=succeeded" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=10" \
  --data-urlencode "created_gte=2026-11-01T00:00:00Z"

Register a webhook endpoint

curl -X POST "$BASE_URL/webhook_endpoints" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://merchant.example.com/webhooks/payments",
    "events": ["payment.succeeded", "payment.failed", "refund.updated"]
  }'

6. Error Codes

The API uses conventional HTTP status codes: 2xx indicates success, 4xx indicates a problem with the request, and 5xx indicates a problem on our side.

HTTPError codeMeaningRecommended action
400parameter_invalidA parameter is missing, malformed, or out of rangeFix the request; check param
401authentication_failedAPI key missing, invalid, or revokedVerify the key and environment
402card_declinedIssuer declined the paymentAsk the customer for another payment method
402insufficient_fundsThe account has insufficient fundsAsk the customer for another payment method
402expired_cardThe card has expiredRequest updated card details
403permission_deniedKey lacks access to this resource or actionUse a key with the right permissions
404resource_not_foundThe object ID does not existCheck the ID and environment
409idempotency_conflictIdempotency key reused with different parametersUse a new key for a new request
409invalid_stateOperation not allowed in the object's current state (e.g. refunding an uncaptured payment)Retrieve the object and check its status
422amount_exceeds_limitAmount exceeds the permitted maximum or refundable balanceReduce the amount
429rate_limitedToo many requestsBack off and retry after Retry-After
500internal_errorUnexpected server errorRetry with the same idempotency key; contact support if persistent
503service_unavailableTemporary outage or maintenanceRetry with exponential backoff
Retry guidance: Retry only 429, 500, and 503 responses, plus network timeouts, and always with the same Idempotency-Key. Do not retry other 4xx errors without changing the request.

7. Webhooks

Webhooks notify your server when events occur, such as a payment succeeding or a refund changing status. Use them rather than polling, since some outcomes (3-D Secure completion, delayed refunds, disputes) happen asynchronously.

Setup

  1. Expose an HTTPS endpoint that accepts POST requests with a JSON body.
  2. Register it in the Dashboard or via POST /webhook_endpoints. The response includes a whsec_ signing secret.
  3. Return a 2xx status within 10 seconds. Do heavy processing asynchronously after acknowledging.

Event types

EventTriggered when
payment.authorizedA manual-capture payment is authorized
payment.succeededA payment is captured successfully
payment.failedA payment attempt fails
payment.canceledA payment is canceled
refund.createdA refund is created
refund.updatedA refund changes status (succeeded or failed)
dispute.createdA customer disputes a charge

Event payload

{
  "id": "evt_1QzR7s0Lm9",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "payment.succeeded",
  "created_at": "2026-11-23T10:15:02Z",
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "pay_3MtwBw2eZvKY",
      "object": "payment",
      "amount": 2500,
      "currency": "usd",
      "status": "succeeded"
    }
  }
}

Verifying signatures

Every webhook includes a Payments-Signature header:

Payments-Signature: t=1795428900,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa51cad7e77a0e56ff536d0ce8e108d8bd

To verify:

  1. Split the header to extract the timestamp t and signature v1.
  2. Build the signed payload: t + "." + the raw request body.
  3. Compute an HMAC-SHA256 of that string using your whsec_ secret.
  4. Compare with v1 using a constant-time comparison, and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes to prevent replay attacks.
// Node.js (Express) example
const crypto = require("crypto");

app.post("/webhooks/payments", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), (req, res) => {
  const header = req.get("Payments-Signature") || "";
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(header.split(",").map(p => p.split("=")));
  const signedPayload = `${parts.t}.${req.body.toString("utf8")}`;

  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET)
    .update(signedPayload)
    .digest("hex");

  const valid =
    parts.v1 &&
    parts.v1.length === expected.length &&
    crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(parts.v1), Buffer.from(expected));
  const fresh = Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(parts.t)) < 300;

  if (!valid || !fresh) return res.status(400).send("Invalid signature");

  const event = JSON.parse(req.body);
  // Enqueue event for async processing, then acknowledge
  res.sendStatus(200);
});

Delivery and retries

  • Non-2xx responses and timeouts are retried with exponential backoff for up to 3 days (about 8 attempts: 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 5 h, 10 h, then every 12 h).
  • Delivery is at least once, and ordering is not guaranteed. De-duplicate using the event id and make handlers idempotent.
  • Endpoints that fail continuously for 7 days are automatically disabled, and you will be notified by email.

8. Rate Limits

Limits are applied per API key to protect platform stability. Exceeding a limit returns 429 rate_limited.

EnvironmentScopeLimit
ProductionAll endpoints (per key)100 requests / second
ProductionPOST /payments50 requests / second
ProductionList endpoints (GET collections)20 requests / second
SandboxAll endpoints (per key)25 requests / second

Higher limits are available for high-volume merchants; contact support to request an increase.

Rate limit headers

HeaderDescription
X-RateLimit-LimitMaximum requests allowed in the current window
X-RateLimit-RemainingRequests remaining in the current window
X-RateLimit-ResetUnix timestamp when the window resets
Retry-AfterSeconds to wait before retrying (only on 429)

Example 429 response

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1795428902

{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_error",
    "code": "rate_limited",
    "message": "Too many requests. Retry after 2 seconds.",
    "request_id": "req_2Xb9PqLd01"
  }
}

Best practices

  • Honor Retry-After and use exponential backoff with jitter.
  • Prefer webhooks over polling to reduce request volume.
  • Use cursor pagination with the maximum limit of 100 rather than many small requests.
  • Smooth out batch jobs with a client-side queue or token bucket.
Go-live checklist: switch to sk_live_ keys and the production base URL; verify webhook signatures; send idempotency keys on every POST; handle 402 declines gracefully; and log every request_id.
